Markdown reads a line lazy to a quote's container as indented less than any block, as markdown-it does (rich-unfiled-791c.emsm)

markdown-it gives a quote's lazy line sCount -1, and a list item's lazy line
sits short of the item's indentation, so a quote inside either checks its
terminators on that line as indented less than four. "> > b\n    ---" is the
quote "b", then indented code at the top level, in Rich 15; it was "b ---"
here. Same for a fence, an HTML block, a heading and a list item.

markdown-it's quote also takes a `>` line after its first at any indentation
("> a\n    > b" is one quote, "a b"), which the same function read as text.
Pinned against Rich 15 (markdown-it-py 4.2).

Markdown lays a quote's content out four cells short of the width, as Rich's BlockQuote does (rich-unfiled-791c.hlmh) (#448)

* Markdown lays a quote's content out four cells short of the width, as Rich's BlockQuote does (rich-unfiled-791c.hlmh)

A quote's text now wraps, rules and justifies at the width less four beside its two-cell bar, so its rows end two cells short, byte for byte with Rich 15's output for wrapped text, a rule, justify and a nested quote.

* Markdown hands a quote's content a cell count, never a negative width (rich-unfiled-791c.hlmh)

Review fixes: the quote's narrowed width goes through cellCount, so a quote at width 0 or 1 no longer passes guttered a negative maxWidth. The quote table's test titles name their options, so the two justify rows are told apart, and the older bar test it duplicated is gone. The one-cell floor in guttered that departs from Rich at narrow widths is rich-unfiled-791c.jra3.
